To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
loss of heterozygositiy (LOH) was detected in 69% of childhood ALL cases and was significantly associated with the clinical outcome of the patients, especially with the 12p LO.
LOH of 6q and 9p was associated with poor prognosis in childhood ALL, and LOH of 12p was associated with a good prognosis.
LOH of 6q and 12q is associated with a good outcome, while 9p and 11q are related to a poor outcome in ALL patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical significance of LOH in childhood ALL.
the identification of the genetic alterations in ALL and the correlation of LOH with clinical features.
the study of the prognostic value of LOH in ALL, which is of great interest for the design of new therapeutic strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the loss of 6q is an unfavorable marker, the loss of 9p is an unfavorable marker in T cell ALL, the loss of chromosome 11q is an indicator of a good response to chemotherapy, and the loss of 12p is a favorable prognostic marker.
6q LOHI is associated with a poor prognosis, 9p LOHI with a poor outcome, 12p LOHI with better prognosis and 11q LOHI is not a prognostic marker in childhood ALL.
LOH of 9p is the most common alteration in childhood ALL; 6q and 11q alterations are less frequent; and 12p alterations are rare.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LOH of 6q and 9p was associated with poor prognosis, while LOH of 11q and, to a lesser extent 12p, was associated with good prognosis.
LOH of 6q and 12q is associated with a good prognosis, whereas 9p LOh and 11q LOh are associated with a worse outcome.
LOH is not an isolated event but a complex process, which may involve several chromosomes and may be associated with a poor prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LOH of 6q and 12 p is an indicator of favorable prognosis in this group of patients.
6q and 9p LOHS are independent prognostic factors for childhood ALL.
LOH at chromosome 6q, which is the only site with prognostic significance, is associated with a better prognosis.
